body:
Safeguarding the Wealth of Generations: Atty. Allan Yntig’s Global Milestone in Family Wealth Stewardship

by Casey Andre Que

In the delicate world of family business, wealth is never just about balance sheets, investment portfolios, or corporate holdings. Real family wealth is a living, breathing tapestry of shared history, deep emotions, complex relationships, and the heavy, beautiful responsibility of legacy. Managing it requires a rare bridge of expertise—one that balances the cold, analytical precision of the law with the warm, deeply human realities of family dynamics.

At Premier Family Business Consulting, we are profoundly honored and incredibly proud to announce a monumental milestone in this journey of stewardship. Atty. Allan Yntig has officially been awarded the prestigious FFI GEN (Global Educational Network) Certificate in Family Wealth Advising (CFWA) by the world-renowned Family Firm Institute (FFI).

This global certification is not merely a professional credential. It is a distinction presented only to individuals who have achieved a profound, comprehensive level of professional knowledge and gained significant, practical expertise that directly translates into transformative value for family business owners and family wealth clients.

The Art and Science of Sustainable Wealth

For next-generation leaders and current family business owners alike, transitioning from a bustling, day-to-day operating business to managing shared, multi-generational family assets is one of the most volatile phases an enterprise can face. It is the exact point where many legacies fracture.

Through the rigorous curriculum of the FFI GEN Certificate in Family Wealth Advising, Atty. Allan has sharpened his expertise in the specialized frameworks necessary to navigate these exact waters safely. His advanced training equips him to guide families through:

  • Diverse Models of Family Wealth: Understanding that true wealth comprises financial, human, social, and intellectual capital.

  • The Transition Stage: Masterfully guiding families as they shift their focus from running a singular operational business to stewarding a complex, shared ecosystem of assets.

  • Systems Theory in Action: Viewing the family, the business, and the ownership not as isolated parts, but as a deeply interconnected system where a ripple in one area affects all others.

  • The Human "Soft" Skills: Applying specialized advising skills—specifically advanced facilitation, open communication, and constructive conflict resolution—to keep family bonds intact while wealth grows.

A Champion for Sustainable Stewardship

What makes Atty. Allan’s achievement so vital to our community is how he translates this world-class knowledge into local, heart-centered impact. In a landscape where family enterprises represent the backbone of our economy, having an advisor who holds both a sharp legal mind and a globally certified grasp of family wealth dynamics is a rare shield for any family legacy.

Atty. Allan does not merely advise on structures; he champions sustainable stewardship. He helps families look past the immediate horizon to ask the hard, necessary questions: How do we prepare our children to be responsible stewards, rather than just consumers of wealth? How do we build a governance system that honors our founders' values while giving the next generation room to lead?

"True wealth preservation is not about building walls around assets. It is about building bridges of trust, clarity, and shared purpose across generations."

Elevating the Premier Standard

By achieving the CFWA certification from the Family Firm Institute, Atty. Allan joins an elite global network of multi-disciplinary professionals dedicated to the longevity of family enterprises. For our clients at Premier, this means direct access to international best practices tailored specifically to the unique nuances, cultural values, and emotional realities of our local family businesses.

Your Premier family stands united in celebrating this remarkable milestone. We thank Atty. Allan for his tireless dedication to continuous learning, his pursuit of excellence, and his unwavering commitment to helping families in business thrive across generations.

Congratulations, Atty. Allan Yntig, CFWA! Thank you for continually inspiring sustainable stewardship and lighting the path toward legacies that stand the test of time.

body:
Christian Stewart's the Value of family Meetings During Pandemic

by Maria Chonita Rivera - Cejas

The disruption of the recent global pandemic brought with it a profound paradox—a heavy, quiet season that forced us to face both the implausible and the possible. In a world suddenly tilted on its axis, we were given a rare, albeit difficult, invitation: to Pause, to Praise, to Pivot, and to Pursue the true meaning of Life’s Purpose.

Amidst the noise of shifting economies and global uncertainty, a singular, anchoring question emerged in the hearts of leaders and founders everywhere: For whom do we live?

More than ever, the answer has returned us to our roots. The word and the dedication for FAMILY have been thrust beautifully to the fore. We realized that our businesses, our assets, and our daily hustles are merely the scaffolding; the family itself is the masterpiece.

During the Asian Family Enterprise Excellence Conference (AFEEC), Christian Stewart, the visionary Managing Director of Family Legacy Asia (HK) Limited, captured this global shift perfectly. In his address, he shared a powerful observation: families are "evidently and intentionally finding time to connect."

At the heart of this intentional connection lies a deceptively simple, yet transformative practice that Stewart championed as vital: The Family Meeting.

What is a Family Meeting? Moving Beyond the Boardroom

For many business-owning families, meetings are synonymous with financial reports, operational targets, and legal structures. But a true Family Meeting is entirely different. It is not a boardroom negotiation; it is a sacred space.

The Center for Parenting Education offers a beautifully grounded definition:

Family meetings are structured, collaborative discussions that involve all family members who are concerned about or affected by a particular issue.

It is an intentional gathering where the hierarchy of the business is temporarily set aside, allowing members to meet simply as mothers, fathers, brothers, sisters, and partners.

The Infinite Agenda: From the Simple to the Strategic

One of the most beautiful aspects of the family meeting is its versatility. There is no rigid template, because no two families are identical. The agenda of a family meeting can carry a myriad of topics, adapting organically to the season the family is walking through:

1. Celebrations and Legacy Milestones

Sometimes, a meeting is simply a designated Time Together. It is a space to discuss family experiences, celebrate personal milestones, plan the next family trip, or recount the founding generation's stories so they are woven into the hearts of the youngest members.

2. Alignment and Vision Casting

A family meeting is a safe harbor to discuss shifts in family civil status—such as welcoming new in-laws or celebrating new births—and to gently align everyone on how these changes fit into the broader family narrative. It ensures that everyone feels seen, heard, and valued.

3. Proactive Problem Solving and Preservation

Rather than waiting for a crisis to strike, healthy families use meetings for preventative stewardship. It is a safe sandbox for problem identification, brainstormed solutions, and the proactive prevention of future conflicts. By talking through potential issues today, families build the structural and emotional muscle needed to weather tomorrow's storms.

The Value of the Meeting in Times of Transition

When crisis or rapid change hits, isolation is the enemy of continuity. When family members do not communicate, assumptions fill the silence, and assumptions are the breeding ground for misunderstanding and division.

As Christian Stewart highlighted, the pandemic proved that intentional connection is not a luxury—it is a survival mechanism. The families that emerged stronger from the crisis were not those with the most flawless balance sheets, but those who paused to sit in a circle, looked each other in the eye, and asked: "How are we doing, and how do we navigate this together?"

This is where sustainable stewardship begins. By institutionalizing the family meeting, next-generation family business owners learn the art of collective decision-making. They learn that while the business belongs to the market, the legacy belongs to the family.

A Call for the Next-Gen Leaders

To the next generation of family business owners and leaders: the legacy you inherit is only as strong as the relationships that support it.

We challenge you to initiate this simple practice. Do not wait for a corporate crisis or a family emergency to call everyone to the table. Let your next meeting be a celebration of your shared bond, a moment to pause, and a collective commitment to keep pursuing your family’s unique purpose—together.

body:
Professor Toshio Goto. Source IMD Business School

The Secrets of the Thousand-Year Heritage: Lessons in Business Longevity with Professor Toshio Goto

by Ruby Joy Limbaga

In a fast-paced global economy obsessed with the next quarter's earnings, rapid scaling, and overnight tech unicorns, the concept of long-term survival is often pushed to the margins. Businesses are built to scale, sold for profit, or dissolved in the face of market disruption. Yet, there is a quiet, powerful counter-narrative whispered across centuries: the story of the Shinise—the ancient, multi-centennial family enterprises that have survived wars, natural disasters, economic collapses, and global pandemics.

While years have passed since the landmark Asian Family Enterprise Excellence Conference (AFEEC), its lessons remain incredibly vital and timeless. Among the most memorable and inspiring sessions was the masterclass delivered by Professor Toshio Goto, the pioneering legend of family business research in Japan.

With data that challenged modern corporate assumptions, Professor Goto illuminated a beautiful truth: the ultimate masters of business longevity are, and have always been, family-owned enterprises

The Mind-Boggling Scale of Japan’s Centennial Giants

To ground his research, Professor Goto presented statistics that are as staggering as they are inspiring. Japan is home to the highest concentration of long-surviving businesses in the world. He shared that within the country:

  • 52,328 firms have successfully operated for over a century.

  • 1,938 firms have survived and thrived for over five hundred years.

  • 21 legendary enterprises have been in continuous operation for over one thousand years.

These are not merely static organizations preserved in time. They are active, evolving businesses that have continually navigated change while keeping their core values entirely intact.

To help give these massive numbers a human touch and translate academic data into living reality, Professor Goto introduced a special guest to the virtual stage: Yoshiaki Matsumura, the CEO of the Japan Flower Corporation.

A Living Legacy: The Japan Flower Corporation

As Yoshiaki Matsumura spoke about his family business—which proudly numbers among the centennial firms of Japan—the conference attendees caught a rare glimpse into the daily heartbeat of a Shinise.

For the Japan Flower Corporation, surviving for over a century was never about maximizing raw profit at all costs. Instead, it was about stewardship. Matsumura highlighted that their longevity is built on three core pillars:

1. The Long-Term Horizon

Decisions are not made for the next fiscal year; they are made with the next generation in mind. This long-term perspective allows the business to build deep reserves, avoid reckless debt, and invest in sustainable relationships with suppliers and customers.

2. Adaptation and Evolution

While the core values and the family's ultimate mission remain unshakeable, the methods change. To survive a hundred years, a business must constantly innovate, embrace new technologies, and pivot its operations to meet the needs of a changing society.

3. Community Integration

A Shinise does not exist in a vacuum. It views itself as a vital organ of its community. By prioritizing the well-being of employees, partners, and local neighborhoods, the business builds an armor of goodwill that protects it during economic winters.

Key Takeaways for Next-Gen Family Leaders

Professor Goto’s research offers a roadmap for next-generation family business owners seeking to build their own multi-generational legacies:

Longevity Factor Conventional Business Focus Shinise Family Business Focus
Primary Metric Short-term growth & shareholder ROI Generational succession & stewardship
Risk Appetite Aggressive leverage for rapid expansion Conservative growth with deep cash reserves
Core Philosophy Market dominance and disruption Preservation of trust and long-term relationships

"A business is a trust passed down from the ancestors to be delivered safely, and improved, into the hands of the children."

Building a Legacy That Outlasts the Century

For the families we advise at Premier Family Business Consulting, Professor Goto’s insights serve as both an anchor and a beacon. The path to a hundred years is not paved with luck; it is paved with intentional governance, structured family meetings, and a shared alignment of values.

We extend our deepest gratitude to Professor Toshio Goto and CEO Yoshiaki Matsumura for sharing these priceless lessons. They remind us that while the world changes rapidly, the values of family, trust, and sustainable stewardship are eternal.

Razilee Rae Ligaray and Jefferson Tio Receive Elite Global Distinction in Family Business Advising

by Jefferson Tio

In the global economic landscape, family enterprises stand as the quiet giants. They are the bedrock of community vitality, the engine of job creation, and the fundamental drivers of global economic growth and prosperity. Yet, steering these enterprises across generational lines is an art of extreme complexity. It requires more than standard corporate strategy; it demands an intimate understanding of human behavior, family dynamics, financial structures, and organizational governance.

To guide these families safely into the future, advisors must possess a rare caliber of expertise—one that combines rigorous academic theory with deep, empathetic practice.

It is with immense pride that Premier Family Business Consulting Inc. celebrates a magnificent double milestone. Razilee Rae J. Ligaray and Jefferson M. Tio have both been awarded the highly prestigious FFI GEN (Global Educational Network) Certificate in Family Business Advising (CFBA) by the Family Firm Institute (FFI).

This globally recognized credential is presented only to individuals who have achieved comprehensive professional knowledge and gained significant expertise that can be used as direct, transformative value for family business owners and family wealth clients.

Elevating the Standard of Best Practices

The acquisition of the CFBA distinction is a testament to the relentless pursuit of excellence that defines Premier. By securing this credential, both Razilee and Jefferson ensure that the absolute highest standards in professional best practices will be implemented for the families we serve.

The Family Firm Institute (FFI) designed the GEN Certificate in Family Business Advising specifically to increase awareness and exposure to the concepts, skills, and knowledge necessary to optimize effectiveness as a family business consultant. It is not just an educational course; it is an immersion into the elite mechanics of legacy preservation.

"Through completion of the certificate program, Razilee Rae J. Ligaray and Jefferson M. Tio have gained a deeper understanding of the needs of family-owned enterprises and the many roles family business and non-family members play."

— Judy Green, President of the Family Firm Institute

By mastering the core disciplines of the program—behavioral science, finance, law, and management science—Razilee and Jefferson bring an unparalleled, holistic approach to their consulting work. They are equipped to build collaborative, multi-disciplinary teams that address the complex, overlapping systems of family, ownership, and enterprise.

The Intersection of Science and Heart

What makes this achievement so powerful is the unique blend of perspectives both advisors bring to the table:

With this global certification, Razilee further bridges the gap between academic theory and practical, real-world application. Family businesses are highly nuanced ecosystems, and navigating them requires a disciplined analytical framework. Razilee’s achievement equips her to dissect complex organizational challenges and design structured, sustainable governance models that help next-generation leaders thrive.

Jefferson M. Tio: Cultivating Multi-Generational Trust

As a trusted leader and strategic advocate at Premier, Jefferson’s acquisition of the CFBA certificate deepens his ability to facilitate crucial family conversations. Armed with advanced methodologies from the world’s leading family enterprise association, Jefferson is uniquely positioned to guide families through conflict resolution, succession planning, and the delicate emotional shifts that occur during leadership transitions.

Part of an Elite Global Network

By earning this certificate, Razilee and Jefferson join an elite international community. The Family Firm Institute is the world’s leading professional membership organization for family enterprise professionals, spanning over 1,800 individuals and organizations across 88 countries.

For the clients of Premier Family Business Consulting, this means our advisory services are backed by cutting-edge global research, cross-border insights, and a network of world-class practitioners. We are not just applying local solutions; we are deploying global best practices tailored beautifully to the unique cultural context of our family businesses.

We congratulate Razilee and Jefferson on this stellar achievement. Your Premier family celebrates your dedication to continuous learning, your passion for family business advocacy, and your unwavering commitment to helping the next generation of family owners write their legacy in stone.

Congratulations, Razilee Rae J. Ligaray, CFBA, and Jefferson M. Tio, CFBA! Thank you for continuously elevating the standard of legacy building.
